stem: Suppose that an angle $\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$. Then which of the following statements is correct? ( )
solution: The correct statement is $\sin\alpha = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ — reference angle and quadrant sign give $\sin\alpha = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$. $\sin\alpha = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ is false: the sign is wrong for this quadrant. $\sin\alpha = \dfrac{1}{2}$ is false: that is the value of $\cos\alpha$. $\tan\alpha = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ is false: that is $\dfrac{\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha}$, the reciprocal of the tangent.
form: α = a special angle (QI or QII): which statement is true
